fires.title: COGMF Gold Mountain Fire
fires.unit: Grand Mesa Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests
fires.description: The Gold Mountain Fire was discovered on June 27, 2026, at approximately 5:33 pm 2 miles northeast of Ouray, CO. Fire initially started burning in mixed conifer vegetation located on inaccessible terrain above the east side of Highway 550. Local, State, and Federal initial attack fire resources were ordered immediately. The fire spread quickly running up steep slopes. A local Type 3 Incident Management Team was assigned on June 27, 2026. Aviation resources were ordered throughout the next day, but high winds and terrain features shut down the use of aviation resources. Fire became very active,

fires.title: MTLNF Cherry Peak
fires.description: The Cherry Peak Fire was detected on the afternoon of August 18, 2026. The fire is burning in steep, rugged terrain with timber and grass. Initial fire activity included running and single tree torching. The fire is lightning caused and full suppression tactics are being implemented.The Lolo National Forest Type 3 Organization assumed command of the fire the morning of August 19.Resources ordered and/or supporting the incident: Module and engine crews, large air tankers (LAT), very large airtankers (VLAT), air attack, type one helicopters, type 2 IA crew, smoke jumpers, heli-rappelers, hotshot

fires.title: NMSNF Frijoles Fire
fires.description: The Frijoles Fire, which started August 4th due to a lightning strike, is burning in steep terrain 5 miles west of Sierra Mosca, 3 miles southeast of Cundiyo, NM. Firefighter and public safety are the number 1 objective and the fire is being handled as a full suppression incident.In order to facilitate safe and efficient suppression efforts the public is asked to avoid the area of the fire and the Santa Cruz Overlook Rd and Campground.Aviation operations in support of suppression efforts are occurring at Nambe Lake and Santa Cruz Lake. fires.title: ORFWF Wrights Spring
fires.description: The Wrights Spring Fire was reported on Aug. 5, 2026, in the Fremont-Winema National Forest, south of Sprague River Highway and east of Chiloquin, Ore., between FS 5817 and Rd 22 (Switchback Rd.) NW Team 7 assumed command of the fire August 21, 2026.

fires.title: WAOWF Little Giant Fire
fires.description: Little Giant Fire: It was started by lightning on July 15, is located 30 miles NW of Leavenworth, WA. It is in the Chiwawa River drainage on the Wenatchee River Ranger District of the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. It was originally estimated at 5 acres. Rappellers were dispatched for initial attack, and a 21-person initial attack crew arrived on July 17. Minimal aerial support was available to support firefighters on the ground. Due to winds and increased fire behavior, as well as poor access in steep, inaccessible country, all firefighters disengaged and hiked out on July 18. Warm weath

fires.title: WAMRP Grand Park 2 Fire
fires.description: The Grand Park 2 Fire was reported Aug. 7 and is located approximately three miles north of the Sunrise Visitor Center in Mount Rainier National Park. Local resources managed initial and extended attack until Complex Incident Management Team Northwest 13 assumed command Aug. 11 in coordination with local, state, and federal agencies.

fires.title: MNSUF July 2026 Superior NF Wildfires
fires.description: Notice: As of August 10, incident updates will only be published on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. On the evening of July 6, 2026, a storm system moved through the area with thunder and lightning and little precipitation. The following day, several small wildfires were reported. The Southern Area Complex Incident Management Team 1 is responsible for management of this firefighting effort.For information on Superior National Forest BWCAW openings and closures or fire restrictions, please see the Forest's Alerts webpage: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/superior/alertsThe Little Knife Fire is unde

fires.title: CALPF Timber Fire
fires.description: THIS PAGE IS UPDATED TWICE DAILY.The Timber Fire was detected around 9:30 p.m. Saturday, August 8. After exhibiting moderate overnight growth, it was estimated to be about 45 acres by 7:30 a.m. Sunday, August 9. None of California's eight federal complex incident management teams are immediately available as they are either assigned to other incidents or on mandatory days off. California has strong interagency relationships and coordination; CAL FIRE Incident Management Team 1 is mobilizing and will receive its in-brief Monday afternoon and be delegated command of the fire soon thereafter.Nume

fires.title: WANCP Luna Fire
fires.description: The Luna Fire within the North Cascades National Park Service Complex started in a rock scree southwest of Luna Camp along Big Beaver Trail in steep, rough, and remote terrain. It was discovered on Thursday, July 2, following lightning storms on previous days. The Maine Incident Management Team was assigned to manage this fire beginning on Tuesday, August 4 after significant fire growth occurred. Command of the fire transitioned to Southern Area GRAY Team-1 on Monday, August 17.The Luna Fire is located approximately 12 miles southwest of the Border 2 Fire, also burning within North Cascades Na

fires.title: WAGPF Backbone
fires.description: The Backbone fire is in Gifford Pinchot National Forest, located 7 miles north-east of the town of Packwood, Washington. The Backbone was a lightning caused fire that started on August 5, 2026.

fires.title: IDNCF Moose Mountain
fires.description: Moose Mountain is a wildfire started by lightning and burning approximately 4 miles north of Kelly Forks Campground and Guard Station. The Moose Mountain Fire has burned down to the North Fork of the Clearwater River prompting a closure of that section of Forest Road #250 in Black Canyon.

fires.title: MTFNF Silvertip Fire
fires.description: The Silvertip Fire was started by lightning in the Spotted Bear Ranger District of the Flathead National Forest, approximately 15 miles southeast of Spotted Bear Ranger Station, near Silvertip Mountain. The fire was detected by aircraft on July 24, 2026 while conducting recon on another reported fire. The fire is burning in heavy timber on steep slopes with standing dead and down trees.A Forest Area Closure is in place for the majority of the upper Spotted Bear River drainage for public and firefighter safety: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/flathead/alertsReconnaissance flights continue over the

The fire began on July 16, 2026, following a lightning storm that moved through the area.A Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) is currently in place over the fire to ensure the safety of firefighting aircraft operating on the incident. fires.title: ORUMF Paradise Fire
fires.description: The Paradise Fire is burning in the Umatilla National Forest approximately 18 Miles E of Milton-Freewater, Oregon. The fire began on July 16, 2026, following a lightning storm that moved through the area. A Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) is currently in place over the fire to ensure the safety of firefighting aircraft operating on the incident. Firefighting aircraft and drones are a dangerous combination—unauthorized drones in the vicinity can cause accidents or significantly slow wildfire suppression efforts. Remember: If you fly… we can’t!

fires.title: COGMF Elk Fire
fires.unit: Grand Mesa Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests
fires.description: The 2026 Elk Fire started by lighting on 7-9-2026. The fire continues to burn in remote, rugged wilderness terrain where steep slopes, limited access, and complex terrain present significant risks to firefighters. Because of these conditions, firefighters are using indirect suppression tactics around the perimeter, allowing crew to work safely while establishing a secure containment footprint. Crews are leveraging natural barriers, roads, and strategic landscape features to build firelines and protect values at risk. Firefighter safety remains the top priority.

fires.title: MTBDF Moose Fire
fires.description: The lightning-caused Moose Fire was detected July 26 approximately 24 miles southwest of Philipsburg, Montana. The fire is burning in timber and areas of heavy dead and downed fuels with changing weather conditions influencing fire behavior throughout the incident. Previously burned areas have also influenced the fire’s growth and behavior across the landscape. Firefighters remain actively engaged across the incident, working to reduce risk and protect the public and nearby communities.

fires.title: MTBDF Sand Creek
fires.description: Located approximately 7.5 miles southeast of Wisdom, the fire was initially reported at 1:45 pm on August 1, 2026 and was estimated at 40 acres. Fire behavior was crowning and torching in live green and dead and down subalpine fir.

fires.title: MTBDF Bobcat Lakes
fires.description: Located approximately 12 miles east of Wisdom, the fire was reported around 2:20 p.m. on July 31 at an estimated six acres and quickly grew in size due to windy and dry conditions. The fire is burning in heavy dead and downed fuels and thick timber.

fires.title: MTFNF Skillet Fire
fires.description: The Skillet Fire was detected in the Tally Lake Ranger District of the Flathead National Forest, roughly 15 miles from Olney, MT in the Bowen Creek area. The fire was reported in the afternoon of July 29, 2026. The fire is burning in heavy timber and dead and down trees. The fire crossed the Kootenai National Forest boundary on July 30. A local Type 3 fire management organization assumed command of the fire on August 18, 2026.All EVACUATION WARNINGS have been lifted and all areas are now CLEAR.

fires.title: IDIPF Upper Smith Fire
fires.description: The Upper Smith Fire is located within the Smith Creek drainage, approximately 6 miles west of Porthill, Idaho and about 20 miles northwest of Bonners Ferry, Idaho. The fire was ignited by lightning on July 7th. It is burning on a steep, north-facing slope in heavy timber with significant concentrations of dead and down fuels.The Northern Idaho Blue Team assumed command of the fire on August 12, 2026, at 6:00 am. A full suppression strategy will continue to be implemented utilizing direct and indirect tactics to protect critical values at-risk and minimize firefighter risk exposure.

fires.title: WAOWF Three Queens
fires.description: Three Queens Facebook (frequent video updates).The Three Queens Fire is located on Okanogan Wenatchee National Forest, six miles east of Snoqualmie Pass, in Kittitas County. The fire is burning primarily in high elevation subalpine fir stringers above Lake Kachess. Wind driven fire behavior persists as strong winds push flames across fuels. Fire activity has increased in areas where fuels, wind, and topography have aligned, producing periods of faster fire spread. This mountainous region also exhibits extreme slopes, unstable terrain and rolling material. Crews are monitoring these conditions

fires.title: WAGPF High Lava Fire
fires.description: The High Lava Fire located approximately 10 miles northwest of Stabler, Washington, continues to remain active. Multiple resources, including hand crews, engines, and heavy equipment, are aggressively engaging the fire under a full suppression strategy. Crews are improving roads, constructing dozer lines, and attacking the fire directly where it is safe to do so. Smoke will be visible near Stabler, WA, and surrounding communities. The High Lava Fire is burning in extremely challenging country, where near-vertical slopes and cliff bands make access difficult for firefighters. Crews remain focus

fires.title: ORUMF Bologna Fire
fires.description: Bologna Fire, seven mile northeast of Kimberly, OR. Started July 16, 2026. The Oregon Department of Forestry (ODF) Complex Incident Management Team (CIMT) 3 took command of the Bologna Fire from a local Type-3 organization and the Cottonwood Fire from a Central Oregon Fire Management Service Team (COFMS) type-3 incident management team.

fires.title: COPSF Aspen Acres Fire
fires.unit: Pike and San Isabel National Forest
fires.description: The Aspen Acres Fire was first reported on June 29th at approximately 6:00am. The fire originated 10 miles northwest of Rye, Colorado in the area of the San Isabel National Forest.The Aspen Acres Fire experienced explosive growth due to record‑low fuel moisture levels and persistent red flag conditions during the week preceding and the days following ignition. The fire was driven by sustained winds over 40 mph, with gusts estimated up to 100 mph. It initially impacted the community of Beulah, Colorado, and later affected additional communities and areas across Custer, Pueblo, Fremont, and Huer

fedreg.title: Proposed Plan of Operations; Joshua Tree National Park, CA
fedreg.description: The National Park Service is giving notice to the public that First Class Miners Inc. has filed a proposed plan to use personal vehicles on two roads within Joshua Tree National Park to reach mining claims located outside the park.

fedreg.title: Special Areas; Roadless Area Conservation
fedreg.description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA or Department) is proposing to rescind the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule (2001 Roadless Rule), which established broad prohibitions on road construction, road reconstruction, and timber harvesting within inventoried roadless areas on National Forest System lands. fedreg.title: Secure Rural Schools Resource Advisory Committees
fedreg.description: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Forest Service is seeking nominations for the Secure Rural Schools Resource Advisory Committees (RAC) pursuant to the Secure Rural Schools (SRS) and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 and the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA).
